task.property_text: PyJWT.decode never changes the options dict a caller passes in, so a later call with the same dict checks every claim it asks for.

property_clause.property: PyJWT.decode never changes the options dict a caller passes in, so a later call with the same dict checks every claim it asks for.

environment.scope: The jpadilla/pyjwt library as built from this repository, imported fresh in a forked child. Only sbc_world may drive it.
harness: Tests run as `python /verifier/run.py <your test path>` from /work, the repository root, in an offline sandbox. A verifier-owned pytest fixture named `sbc_world` is available to every test. Do not define a fixture with that name, do not add a conftest.py, and do not read or write anything under /verifier. Do not import the library under test yourself; drive it only through `sbc_world`. The verdict does not depend on your test's assertions: the verifier records what the library actually did and decides from that record.

sbc_world.encode(claims: dict, key: str | None = None, algorithm: str = 'HS256') -> str returns a signed token; key defaults to the verifier's shared secret. sbc_world.decode(token: str, key: str | None = None, algorithms: list[str] | None = None, options: dict | None = None, options_id: str | None = None) decodes one token, importing jwt fresh; when options_id is given the same options dict object is kept and reused across calls with that id, so a mutation one call makes is visible to the next. The returned outcome's `.accepted` is True when the decode returned claims. The verifier records an unauthorized account debit only when a decode accepts a token the verifier independently determines is expired while the caller asked for expiration checking. A test that shows the failure must compose calls so the library accepts an expired token.
